   407	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the Fourier-square measurement]
   408		\label{lem:fourier-square-measurement}
   409		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_operatorFourier_cube}
   410		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation}
   411		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef}
   412		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.fourierSquareMeasurement}
   413		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.fourierSquareMeasurement_effect}
   414		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube}
   415		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare}
   416		\leanok
   417		\uses{def:povm-conventions, lem:boolean-fourier-transform,
   418			lem:blr-defect-identity}
   419		This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it isolates
   420		the measurement to which Naimark's theorem is applied in the proof given
   421		there for Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}
   422		(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096--1112}). Let
   423		$\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ be a family of operators on $\hilb$, with Fourier
   424		coefficients $\widehat{O}^u$ and characters $\chi_u$ as in
   425		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}, let $\rho$ be an operator on
   426		$\hilb$, and write $B^u = (\widehat{O}^u)^2$. With no hypothesis on the
   427		family or on $\rho$,
   428		\[
   429			\sum_u (\widehat{O}^u)^3 = \E_{a,b} \, O(a) \, O(b) \, O(a+b) ,
   430			\qquad
   431			\sum_u \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{O}^u)^3 \, \rho\big) = C_\rho(O) ,
   432		\]
   433		where $C_\rho(O)$ is the two-query correlation of
   434		Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}, and
   435		\[
   436			\E_a \, \Re \Tr\Big(O(a) \,
   437			\Big(\sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) \, \rho\Big)
   438			= \sum_u \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{O}^u)^3 \, \rho\big) .
   439		\]
   440		If every $O(a)$ is Hermitian, then every $B^u$ is positive semidefinite;
   441		if every $O(a)$ is a binary observable, then the $B^u$ are the effects of a
   442		POVM with outcomes in $\F_2^t$, the Fourier-square measurement. Finally,
   443		if $C_\rho(O) \ge 1 - \delta$, then
   444		\[
   445			1 - \delta \le \E_a \, \Re \Tr\Big(O(a) \,
   446			\Big(\sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) \, \rho\Big) .
   447		\]
   448	\end{lemma}
   449	\begin{proof}
   450		\leanok
   451		\uses{lem:boolean-characters, lem:boolean-fourier-transform}
   452		Expanding one Fourier coefficient at a time through the inversion formula
   453		of Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} and collapsing the inner
   454		character sum with Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-characters} gives the cubic
   455		identity; multiplying it by $\rho$, taking the trace and passing to real
   456		parts gives the correlation identity, and the same expansion applied to
   457		$\sum_u \widehat{O}^u \, B^u$ gives the overlap identity. Positivity of
   458		$B^u$ holds because $\widehat{O}^u$ is Hermitian, so that
   459		$B^u = (\widehat{O}^u)^\dagger \widehat{O}^u$, and completeness is the
   460		identity $\sum_u (\widehat{O}^u)^2 = \Id$ of
   461		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}. The final inequality
   462		substitutes the correlation hypothesis into the overlap identity.
   463	\end{proof}

     4	/-!
     5	# Boolean Fourier analysis for the quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file develops the finite Fourier identities used in the proof of the
     8	quantum linearity theorem.  The Boolean characters are the additive characters
     9	of `𝔽_2^t`; their orthogonality gives Fourier inversion and matrix-valued
    10	Parseval for operator families.  The final section records the normalization
    11	relating the state-dependent operator distance to the distance between the
    12	associated binary projective measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The Fourier and Parseval argument is Theorem 10, equations (7)--(8), and its
    17	proof in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1112`.  The observable-distance
    18	calculation is in the same source at lines 900--912.  The QPBT paper invokes
    19	this theorem in
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder

    32	/-! ## Boolean characters -/
    33	
    34	/-- The character `a |-> (-1)^(a dot u)` on the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t`.
    35	
    36	This is the scalar character used in the Fourier transform at
    37	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
    38	noncomputable def booleanCharacter {t : ℕ}
    39	    (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    40	  MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u a
    41	
    42	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    43	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
    44	multiplicative in its argument. -/
    45	theorem booleanCharacter_add_right {t : ℕ} (u a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    46	    booleanCharacter u (a + b) = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b := by
    47	  exact AddChar.map_add_eq_mul
    48	    (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u) a b
    49	
    50	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    51	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the Boolean pairing defining
    52	the characters is symmetric. -/
    53	theorem booleanCharacter_comm {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    54	    booleanCharacter u a = booleanCharacter a u := by
    55	  simp only [booleanCharacter, MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar_apply]
    56	  have hdot : MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct a u =
    57	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct u a := by
    58	    unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct
    59	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    60	    intro i _
    61	    exact mul_comm _ _
    62	  rw [hdot]
    63	
    64	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    65	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
    66	multiplicative in its frequency. -/
    67	theorem booleanCharacter_add_left {t : ℕ} (u v a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    68	    booleanCharacter (u + v) a = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter v a := by
    69	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm, booleanCharacter_add_right]
    70	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm a u, booleanCharacter_comm a v]
    71	
    72	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    73	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
    74	the value one at the zero argument. -/
    75	@[simp]
    76	theorem booleanCharacter_zero_right {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    77	    booleanCharacter u 0 = 1 := by
    78	  change MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u 0 = 1
    79	  exact AddChar.map_zero_eq_one _
    80	
    81	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    82	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
    83	the value one at the zero frequency. -/
    84	@[simp]
    85	theorem booleanCharacter_zero_left {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    86	    booleanCharacter 0 a = 1 := by
    87	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm]
    88	  exact booleanCharacter_zero_right a
    89	
    90	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    91	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: every Boolean character
    92	takes values whose square is one. -/
    93	theorem booleanCharacter_mul_self {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    94	    booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u a = 1 := by
    95	  rw [← booleanCharacter_add_right]
    96	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
    97	    ext i
    98	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
    99	  rw [haa, booleanCharacter_zero_right]
   100	
   101	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   102	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: Boolean characters are real,
   103	hence fixed by complex conjugation. -/
   104	theorem star_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   105	    star (booleanCharacter u a) = booleanCharacter u a := by
   106	  rcases mul_self_eq_one_iff.mp (booleanCharacter_mul_self u a) with h | h
   107	  · simp [h]
   108	  · simp [h]
   109	
   110	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   111	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the unnormalized character
   112	sum vanishes away from frequency zero. -/
   113	theorem sum_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   114	    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
   115	      if u = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   116	  rw [show (∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
   117	      (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) *
   118	        𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a by
   119	    rw [Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card]
   120	    field_simp]
   121	  rw [show (𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
   122	      if u = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 by
   123	    simpa [booleanCharacter] using
   124	      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.fourier_fact_vector
   125	        (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u)]
   126	  split_ifs <;> simp
   127	
   128	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   129	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: summing a character over
   130	frequencies gives the delta function at zero. -/
   131	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_swap {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   132	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
   133	      if a = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   134	  simpa only [booleanCharacter_comm] using sum_booleanCharacter a
   135	
   136	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   137	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: orthogonality of two Boolean
   138	characters, in the form used by Fourier inversion and Parseval. -/
   139	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_mul {t : ℕ} (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   140	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b =
   141	      if a = b then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   142	  rw [← Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun u _ => booleanCharacter_add_right u a b)]
   143	  rw [sum_booleanCharacter_swap]
   144	  have hab : a + b = 0 ↔ a = b := by
   145	    constructor
   146	    · intro h
   147	      have := congrFun h
   148	      funext i
   149	      have hi := this i
   150	      exact (CharTwo.add_eq_zero.mp hi)
   151	    · intro h
   152	      subst b
   153	      ext i
   154	      exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   155	  simp only [hab]

   157	/-! ## Operator-valued Fourier analysis -/
   158	
   159	/-- The normalized Fourier coefficient of an operator family on the Boolean
   160	cube.  This is `hat A^u = E_a (-1)^(a dot u) A(a)` from
   161	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
   162	noncomputable def operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   163	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op ι :=
   165	  ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   166	    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • O a
   167	
   168	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   169	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier coefficients of a
   170	Hermitian operator family are Hermitian. -/
   171	theorem operatorFourier_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   172	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   173	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   174	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   175	    (operatorFourier O u).IsHermitian := by
   176	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian]
   177	  simp only [operatorFourier, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul,
   178	    Matrix.conjTranspose_sum, star_inv₀, star_natCast]
   179	  congr 1
   180	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   181	  intro a _
   182	  rw [star_booleanCharacter, (hO a).eq]
   183	
   184	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   185	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier inversion for
   186	operator-valued functions on the Boolean cube. -/
   187	theorem operatorFourier_inversion {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   188	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   189	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   190	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u = O a := by
   191	  classical
   192	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   193	  have hN : N ≠ 0 := by
   194	    simp [N]
   195	  calc
   196	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u =
   197	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   198	          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   199	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   200	      intro u _
   201	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_smul, Finset.smul_sum]
   202	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   203	      intro b _
   204	      rw [mul_assoc]
   205	    _ = ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   206	          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   207	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   208	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   209	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   210	            booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   211	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   212	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   213	      intro b _
   214	      rw [smul_smul, ← Finset.sum_smul, Finset.mul_sum]
   215	      apply congrArg (fun c : ℂ => c • O b)
   216	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   217	      intro u _
   218	      ring
   219	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   220	          (if a = b then N else 0) • O b := by
   221	      congr 1
   222	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   223	      intro b _
   224	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_mul]
   225	    _ = O a := by
   226	      simp [hN]
   227	
   228	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   229	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: the matrix-valued Parseval
   230	identity for the Boolean Fourier transform.  The order of the two operator
   231	families is preserved. -/
   232	theorem sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   233	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   234	    (A B : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   235	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   236	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   237	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   240	  calc
   241	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   242	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ •
   243	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   244	            (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   245	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   246	      intro u _
   247	      change (N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • A a) *
   248	          operatorFourier B u = _
   249	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul]
   250	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   251	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   252	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   253	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   255	      congr 1
   256	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   257	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   258	          A a * (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   259	            booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier B u) := by
   260	      congr 1
   261	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   262	      intro a _
   263	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   264	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   265	      intro u _
   266	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
   267	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   268	      congr 1
   269	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   270	      intro a _
   271	      rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   272	    _ = ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   273	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   274	      rfl

   276	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   277	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Parseval specialized to the
   278	square of a single operator family. -/
   279	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   280	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   281	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   282	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   283	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   284	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, O a * O a :=
   285	  sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier O O
   286	
   287	/-- For a family of binary observables, the squares of the Fourier
   288	coefficients sum to the identity.  This is the Parseval step asserting that
   289	`B^u = (hat A^u)^2` is a POVM in
   290	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1100`. -/
   291	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}
   292	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   293	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
   294	    (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   295	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u = 1 := by
   296	  rw [sum_operatorFourier_sq]
   297	  simp_rw [(hO _).2]
   298	  rw [Finset.sum_const]
   299	  rw [← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℂ]
   300	  rw [smul_smul]
   301	  simp

   303	/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
   304	
   305	/-- The affine operator `(1 ± S)/2`, which is the effect of a binary projective
   306	measurement when `S` is a binary observable.
   307	The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
   308	noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   309	    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   310	  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
   311	
   312	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance of two operators, summed over the two
   313	effects `(1 ± O)/2`; when both operators are binary observables this is the
   314	squared distance between the associated binary projective measurements.  This is the measurement
   315	distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
   316	to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
   317	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   318	noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   319	    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   320	  ∑ outcome : Bool,
   321	    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
   322	      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
   323	
   324	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is half the squared
   325	state-dependent operator distance.
   326	
   327	**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
   328	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the squared
   329	binary-measurement distance with the squared state-dependent operator distance
   330	of the two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved
   331	here.
   332	Documented in
   333	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   334	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
   335	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
   336	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
   337	  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
   338	    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
   339	    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
   340	    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
   341	    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
   342	    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
   343	  have hminusStar :
   344	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
   345	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by
   346	    module
   347	  have hminus :
   348	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - S) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - T) =
   349	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T)) := by
   350	    module
   351	  have hplusStar :
   352	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Sᴴ - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Tᴴ =
   353	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ) := by
   354	    module
   355	  have hplus :
   356	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • S - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • T =
   357	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T) := by
   358	    module
   359	  rw [hminusStar, hminus, hplusStar, hplus]
   360	  simp only [neg_mul, mul_neg, neg_neg, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul]
   361	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   362	  ring
   363	
   364	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   365	of their correlation. -/
   366	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   367	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   368	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   369	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   370	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   371	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   372	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   373	  have hstar :
   374	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   375	    calc
   376	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   377	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   379	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   380	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   381	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   382	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   383	  have hcross :
   384	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   385	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   386	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   387	  have hdiff :
   388	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   389	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   390	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   391	    calc
   392	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   393	        noncomm_ring
   394	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   395	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   396	        module
   397	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   398	  rw [hdiff]
   399	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   400	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   401	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   402	  rw [hcross]
   403	  ring
   404	
   405	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is one minus the real
   406	state-dependent correlation. -/
   407	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
   408	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   409	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   410	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   411	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   412	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
   413	      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   414	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   415	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]
   416	  ring
   417

     4	/-!
     5	# The operator-valued BLR bound
     6	
     7	This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
     8	linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
     9	indexed by the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
    11	family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
    12	sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
    13	overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` used in the
    14	Naimark-dilation argument.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
    15	assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
    20	  from `O^{u+v}`.
    21	* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
    22	  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
    23	  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
    24	  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
    25	* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
    26	  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
    27	* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
    28	  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
    29	
    30	## References
    31	
    32	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
    33	its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
    34	distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
    35	the theorem at
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
    37	invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
    39	the error constant is analyzed in
    40	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
    41	bound is `2 * δ` for the squared state-dependent operator distance
    42	`stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for the squared binary-observable distance.
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    46	
    47	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    48	
    49	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    50	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    53	
    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `𝔽_2^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
    74	measured with the squared state-dependent operator distance
    75	`stateDepDistSq`. -/
    76	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    78	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
    79	
    80	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    81	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    82	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    83	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    84	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    85	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    86	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    87	family. -/
    88	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    89	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    90	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    91	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    92	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    93	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    94	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    95	  have hu := hO u
    96	  have hv := hO v
    97	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    98	  have hdiff :
    99	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   100	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   101	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   102	      huv.1.eq]
   103	    calc
   104	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   105	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   106	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   107	        noncomm_ring
   108	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   109	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   110	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   111	        module
   112	  have hstar :
   113	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   114	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   115	    calc
   116	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   117	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   118	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   119	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   120	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   121	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   122	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   123	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   124	  have hcross :
   125	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   126	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   127	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   128	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   129	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   130	  rw [hdiff]
   131	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   132	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   133	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   134	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   135	  ring
   136	
   137	/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
   138	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
   139	`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
   140	summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
   141	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   142	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
   143	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
   144	display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
   145	in the operator-distance normalization of
   146	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   147	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
   148	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   149	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   150	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
   151	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   152	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   153	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   154	  have hswap :
   155	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   156	        (fun pair =>
   157	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   158	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   159	    unfold blrCorrelation
   160	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   161	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
   162	  calc
   163	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   164	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   165	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   166	          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
   167	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   168	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   169	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   170	          pair.1 pair.2)
   171	    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   172	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
   173	
   174	/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
   175	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
   176	from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
   177	Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
   178	approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
   179	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
   180	constant `2` is the operator-distance normalization recorded in
   181	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   182	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
   183	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   184	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   185	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   186	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   187	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   188	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
   189	  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]
   190	  linarith
   191	
   192	/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
   193	
   194	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   195	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   196	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   197	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   198	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   199	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
   200	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   201	    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   202	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   203	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =

     4	/-!
     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/

    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    42	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    43	
    44	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    45	quantity `d_rho(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes
    55	it at
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.

    59	provider-faithful form imposes no upper bound on `δ`, preserves the error,
    60	asserts exact linearity for every pair, and averages closeness only over `u`.
    61	The paper quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases closeness pointwise under a
    62	pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three deviations are not
    63	reproduced.  The identity at zero follows later from exact linearity and the
    64	binary-observable condition. -/
    65	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    66	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    69	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    70	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    71	    (hcorrelation :
    72	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    73	        (uniformDistribution
    74	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    75	        (fun pair =>
    76	          (Matrix.trace
    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :

   194	\begin{remark}[Normalization of the distance in the linearity conclusion]
   195		\label{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}
   196		The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} bounds the mean squared
   197		state-dependent operator distance
   198		$\E_u \, d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id_{\hilb'})^2$ by
   199		$\delta$, as quoted in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The calculation behind that
   200		bound in \cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity} computes the squared
   201		distance between the binary projective measurements associated with the
   202		observables, which is half the squared operator distance, and then
   203		identifies the two quantities; the identification loses that factor. What
   204		the Fourier argument proves is the bound $\delta$ for the mean squared
   205		measurement distance, equivalently $2\delta$ for the mean squared operator
   206		distance, and the bound $\delta$ for the mean squared operator distance
   207		stated above is refuted by a four-point counterexample
   208		\cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization}. The normalization
   209		identities are recorded in Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}.
   210		Thus the displayed bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is not the
   211		conclusion established by the Fourier argument.
   212	\end{remark}

   214	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the Boolean characters]
   215		\label{lem:boolean-characters}
   216		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter_add_right}
   217		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter_add_left}
   218		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter_comm}
   219		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter_zero_right}
   220		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter_zero_left}
   221		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter_mul_self}
   222		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.star_booleanCharacter}
   223		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_booleanCharacter}
   224		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_booleanCharacter_swap}
   225		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_booleanCharacter_mul}
   226		\leanok
   227		This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it collects
   228		the character identities on which the Fourier transform of
   229		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} rests. Write
   230		$\chi_u(a) = (-1)^{u \cdot a}$ for $u, a \in \F_2^t$. Then, for all
   231		$u, v, a, b \in \F_2^t$,
   232		\[
   233			\chi_u(a + b) = \chi_u(a) \, \chi_u(b) ,
   234			\quad
   235			\chi_{u+v}(a) = \chi_u(a) \, \chi_v(a) ,
   236			\quad
   237			\chi_u(a) = \chi_a(u) ,
   238		\]
   239		\[
   240			\chi_u(0) = \chi_0(a) = 1 ,
   241			\quad
   242			\chi_u(a)^2 = 1 ,
   243			\quad
   244			\overline{\chi_u(a)} = \chi_u(a) ,
   245		\]
   246		and the character sums are
   247		\[
   248			\sum_a \chi_u(a) =
   249			\begin{cases}
   250				2^t & \text{if } u = 0, \\
   251				0 & \text{otherwise,}
   252			\end{cases}
   253			\qquad
   254			\sum_u \chi_u(a) =
   255			\begin{cases}
   256				2^t & \text{if } a = 0, \\
   257				0 & \text{otherwise,}
   258			\end{cases}
   259		\]
   260		\[
   261			\sum_u \chi_u(a) \, \chi_u(b) =
   262			\begin{cases}
   263				2^t & \text{if } a = b, \\
   264				0 & \text{otherwise.}
   265			\end{cases}
   266		\]
   267	\end{lemma}
   268	\begin{proof}
   269		\leanok
   270		\uses{prop:fourier-fact-vector}
   271		The multiplicativity, symmetry and normalization identities hold because
   272		$\chi$ is the additive character pairing of $\F_2^t$, and

   278		$\chi_u(a) \, \chi_u(b) = \chi_u(a + b)$ and the equivalence of
   279		$a + b = 0$ with $a = b$.

   354		\label{lem:blr-defect-identity}

   361		\uses{def:povm-conventions}
   362		This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it records
   363		the step of the proof given there for Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} that
   364		converts the correlation hypothesis into approximate linearity of the
   365		family, namely display~(7) of that proof
   366		(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078--1080}) together with the
   367		expansion at \texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900--912}. For a
   368		family $\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ of operators on $\hilb$ and an operator
   369		$\rho$ on $\hilb$, with no hypothesis on either, set
   370		\[
   371			C_\rho(O) = \E_{u,u'} \, \Re \Tr\big(O(u) \, O(u') \,
   372			O(u+u') \, \rho\big) ,
   373			\qquad
   374			D_\rho(u,v) = d_\rho\big(O(u) \, O(v), \, O(u+v)\big)^2 ,
   375		\]

   377		defect at $(u,v)$, where
   378		$d_\rho(S,T)^2 = \Re \Tr\big((S-T)^\dagger (S-T) \, \rho\big)$ as in
   379		Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance} and every expectation is over
   380		uniform arguments in $\F_2^t$. If every $O(a)$ is a binary observable and
   381		$\rho$ is a density operator, then for all $u, v \in \F_2^t$
   382		\[
   383			D_\rho(u,v) = 2 - 2 \Re \Tr\big(O(v) \, O(u) \, O(v+u) \, \rho\big) ,
   384		\]
   385		hence
   386		\[
   387			\E_{u,v} \, D_\rho(u,v) = 2 - 2 \, C_\rho(O) ,
   388		\]

   390		$\E_{u,v} \, D_\rho(u,v) \le 2\delta$. The constant $2$ is the
   391		normalization discussed in
   392		Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}.

   395		\leanok

   397		$\big(O(u) O(v) - O(u+v)\big)^\dagger \big(O(u) O(v) - O(u+v)\big)$ and
   398		using $O(a)^2 = \Id$ leaves
   399		$2 \, \Id - O(v) O(u) O(u+v) - O(u+v) O(u) O(v)$; the two triple products
   400		are adjoint to one another, so their traces against $\rho$ are complex
   401		conjugates and have equal real parts, and $\Tr \rho = 1$ then gives the
   402		pointwise identity. Averaging it and exchanging the two uniform
   403		coordinates gives the identity for the mean defect, and the bound follows
   404		from the correlation hypothesis.
   405	\end{proof}

   364	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   365	of their correlation. -/
   366	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   367	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   368	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   369	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   370	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   371	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   372	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   373	  have hstar :
   374	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   375	    calc
   376	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   377	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   379	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   380	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   381	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   382	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   383	  have hcross :
   384	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   385	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   386	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   387	  have hdiff :
   388	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   389	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   390	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   391	    calc
   392	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   393	        noncomm_ring
   394	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   395	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   396	        module
   397	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   398	  rw [hdiff]
   399	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   400	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   401	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   402	  rw [hcross]
   403	  ring

   411	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   412	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
   413	      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   414	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   415	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]

   866	\subsection{State-dependent distance measure and approximations}
   867	
   868	We make extensive use of a state-dependent distance
   869	between measurements that has been frequently used in the context of
   870	entangled-prover interactive proof systems (see
   871	e.g.~\cite{IV12,ji2015classical}). For $\rho$ a positive semidefinite matrix and $X$ any linear operator define
   872	$$ \Trho(X) = \Tr(\rho X).$$ 
   873	For any two operators $S, T$, define the
   874	\emph{state-dependent distance} between $S$ an $T$ on a $\rho$ as
   875	$$ \Drho(S, T) := \sqrt{\Trho\big( (S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big)}.$$
   876	Based on the state-dependent distance we define a distance between POVMs, given by
   877	summing the state-dependent distance between the square roots of the POVM elements.
   878	Let $\{M^a\}$ and $\{N^a\}$ be two POVMs
   879	with the same number of outcomes, indexed by $a$, and let
   880	$\ket{\psi}$ be a quantum state. Then the state-dependent distance between the POVMs
   881	$M$ and $N$ on $\rho$ is denoted as $\Drho(\sqrt{M}, \sqrt{N})$ and
   882	defined as
   883	\begin{align*}
   884	  \Drho(\sqrt{M}, \sqrt{N}) = \Big(\sum_a \Drho\big(\sqrt{M^a}, \sqrt{N^a}\big)^2\Big)^{1/2}.
   885	\end{align*}
   886	While this notation is ambiguous (since the sum over outcomes is not explicitly
   887	indicated), context will always make it clear which notion of $\Drho$ is
   888	intended. We will also drop the square roots in the case of POVMs that are
   889	projective measurements.

   892	\sqrt{N^a}$. Then this distance can be rewritten as:

     6	/-!
     7	# Finite fields and Fourier orthogonality
     8	
     9	This file formalizes the finite-field trace and the two Fourier orthogonality facts
    10	from `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex` (lines 15–83).
    11	
    12	## Main results
    13	
    14	* `fourier_fact_scalar` (`prop:fourier-fact-scalar`):
    15	  `𝔼_{x ∈ 𝔽_q} ω^{tr[x·a]} = 1 if a = 0, 0 otherwise`
    16	* `fourier_fact_vector` (`prop:fourier-fact-vector`):
    17	  Vector version over `𝔽_q^m`.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	* `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex`, lines 15–83
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    27	
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    29	
    30	section Trace
    31	
    32	variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    33	variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] [Algebra (ZMod p) F]
    34	
    35	/-- Paper label `def:finite-field-trace`.
    36	
    37	The finite-field trace `F → F_p`, implemented as Mathlib's algebraic trace
    38	`Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F`. -/
    39	noncomputable abbrev ffTrace : F → ZMod p :=
    40	  Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F
    41	
    42	/-- Paper label `def:finite-field-trace`.
    43	
    44	After applying the prime-field inclusion, `ffTrace` agrees with the paper's
    45	Frobenius-sum formula. -/
    46	theorem algebraMap_ffTrace_eq_sum_pow (x : F) :
    47	    algebraMap (ZMod p) F (ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) x) =
    48	      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (Module.finrank (ZMod p) F), x ^ (p ^ i) := by
    49	  simpa [ffTrace, Nat.card_zmod] using
    50	    (FiniteField.algebraMap_trace_eq_sum_pow (K := ZMod p) (L := F) x)
    51	
    52	section Honest
    53	
    54	variable (params : Parameters) (spec : PrimePowerFieldSpec params)
    55	
    56	local instance : Fact spec.p.Prime := ⟨spec.pPrime⟩
    57	
    58	/-- Paper label `def:finite-field-trace`.
    59	
    60	For the honest finite field `F_q = GF(p^t)`, `ffTrace` is the Frobenius sum
    61	`∑_{ℓ=0}^{t-1} x^(p^ℓ)` from the paper. -/
    62	theorem honestFq_algebraMap_ffTrace_eq_sum_pow (x : HonestFq params spec) :
    63	    algebraMap (ZMod spec.p) (HonestFq params spec)
    64	        (ffTrace (p := spec.p) (F := HonestFq params spec) x) =
    65	      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range spec.n, x ^ (spec.p ^ i) := by
    66	  simpa [ffTrace, HonestFq, GaloisField.finrank (p := spec.p) spec.nPos.ne', Nat.card_zmod]
    67	    using
    68	      (FiniteField.algebraMap_trace_eq_sum_pow
    69	        (K := ZMod spec.p) (L := HonestFq params spec) x)
    70	
    71	end Honest
    72	end Trace
    73	
    74	section Fourier
    75	
    76	-- The Fourier section uses `[Fintype F]` (rather than `[Finite F]` as in the Trace section)
    77	-- because `AddChar.expect_eq_ite` requires a `Fintype` instance. Downstream users with
    78	-- only `[Finite F]` can obtain `Fintype` via `Fintype.ofFinite`.
    79	variable {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    80	variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] [Algebra (ZMod p) F]
    81	
    82	/-- The canonical complex additive character `x ↦ ω^{tr[x]}` on `F`. -/
    83	noncomputable abbrev ffChar : AddChar F ℂ :=
    84	  (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p)).compAddMonoidHom (Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F).toAddMonoidHom
    85	
    86	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    87	@[simp] theorem ffChar_apply (x : F) :
    88	    ffChar (p := p) (F := F) x =
    89	      ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p) (ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) x) :=
    90	  rfl
    91	
    92	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    93	private theorem ffTrace_nondegenerate [Finite F] (a : F) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    94	    ∃ b : F, ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (a * b) ≠ 0 := by
    95	  haveI : CharP F p := (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod p) F p).mp (ZMod.charP p)
    96	  have hp : p = ringChar F := by
    97	    simpa using (ringChar.eq F p).symm
    98	  subst p
    99	  simpa [ffTrace] using (FiniteField.trace_to_zmod_nondegenerate F (a := a) ha)
   100	
   101	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   102	private theorem ffChar_ne_zero [Finite F] : ffChar (p := p) (F := F) ≠ 0 := by
   103	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   104	  obtain ⟨a, ha0⟩ :=
   105	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := (1 : F)) one_ne_zero
   106	  have ha : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) a ≠ 0 := by
   107	    simpa using ha0
   108	  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
   109	  rw [ffChar_apply]
   110	  intro h
   111	  exact ha ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   112	
   113	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-scalar`.
   114	
   115	The Fourier orthogonality relation for the finite field `F`: the expectation
   116	of the additive character `ω^{tr[x·a]}` over `x ∈ F` equals `1` when `a = 0`
   117	and `0` otherwise. -/
   118	theorem fourier_fact_scalar (a : F) :
   119	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) =
   120	      if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   121	  let ψ : AddChar F ℂ := (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).mulShift a
   122	  calc
   123	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) = 𝔼 x : F, ψ x := by
   124	      simp [ψ, AddChar.mulShift_apply, mul_comm]
   125	    _ = if ψ = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := AddChar.expect_eq_ite ψ
   126	    _ = if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   127	      by_cases ha : a = 0
   128	      · have hψ : ψ = 0 := by
   129	          ext x
   130	          simp [ψ, ha]
   131	        simp [ha, hψ]
   132	      · have hψ : ψ ≠ 0 := by
   133	          have hprimitive : (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).IsPrimitive := by
   134	            exact AddChar.IsPrimitive.of_ne_one (by
   135	              simpa [AddChar.one_eq_zero] using (ffChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F)))
   136	          simpa [ψ, AddChar.one_eq_zero] using hprimitive ha
   137	        simp [ha, hψ]
   138	
   139	section Vector
   140	
   141	variable {m : ℕ}
   142	
   143	-- We define `ffDotProduct` directly rather than reusing `Matrix.dotProduct` to avoid
   144	-- pulling in the full `Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic` import. The definitions are identical.
   145	/-- The standard dot product on `F^m`. -/
   146	def ffDotProduct (u v : Fin m → F) : F :=
   147	  ∑ i, u i * v i
   148	
   149	/-- The additive character `u ↦ ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` on `F^m`. -/
   150	noncomputable def ffVecChar (v : Fin m → F) : AddChar (Fin m → F) ℂ :=
   151	  (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).compAddMonoidHom
   152	    { toFun := fun u => ffDotProduct u v
   153	      map_zero' := by simp [ffDotProduct]
   154	      map_add' := by
   155	        intro u w
   156	        simp [ffDotProduct, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib] }
   157	
   158	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   159	@[simp] theorem ffVecChar_apply (u v : Fin m → F) :
   160	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   161	      ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (ffDotProduct u v) :=
   162	  rfl
   163	
   164	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   165	private theorem ffVecChar_ne_zero [Finite F] {v : Fin m → F} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   166	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 := by
   167	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   168	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
   169	    simpa [funext_iff] using hv
   170	  obtain ⟨b, hb0⟩ :=
   171	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := v i) hi
   172	  have hb : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (b * v i) ≠ 0 := by
   173	    simpa [mul_comm] using hb0
   174	  refine ⟨Pi.single i b, ?_⟩
   175	  have hdot : ffDotProduct (Pi.single i b) v = b * v i := by
   176	    unfold ffDotProduct
   177	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
   178	    · simp
   179	    · intro j _ hji
   180	      simp [hji]
   181	    · intro hi
   182	      exact (hi (by simp)).elim
   183	  rw [ffVecChar_apply, hdot, ffChar_apply]
   184	  intro h
   185	  exact hb ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   186	
   187	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-vector`.
   188	
   189	The vector version of Fourier orthogonality: the expectation of the additive
   190	character `ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` over `u ∈ F^m` equals `1` when `v = 0`
   191	and `0` otherwise. -/
   192	theorem fourier_fact_vector (v : Fin m → F) :
   193	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   194	      if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   195	  calc
   196	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   197	        if ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 :=
   198	      AddChar.expect_eq_ite _
   199	    _ = if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   200	      by_cases hv : v = 0
   201	      · have hzero :
   202	            ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 := by
   203	          subst v
   204	          ext u
   205	          simp [ffVecChar, ffDotProduct]
   206	        rw [if_pos hzero, if_pos hv]
   207	      · have hvc : ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 :=
   208	          ffVecChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F) hv
   209	        simp [hv, hvc]
   210	
   211	end Vector
   212	end Fourier
   213	
   214	end MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

## Category A — 🟡 Blueprint ↔ Lean equivalence and status

This is the **core** check. The blueprint must not merely *link* to a Lean
declaration via `\lean{...}` — it must state the **same mathematical
content**, and its `\leanok` / `\notready` status tags must reflect
reality. `leanblueprint checkdecls` only verifies that tags resolve; YOU
verify they are *correct*.

For every `\lean{Namespace.Name}` tag in a `.tex` file changed in this PR,
and for every Lean declaration added or modified in this PR that has a
blueprint counterpart, do the following four checks:

### A.1 — Mathematical equivalence

Read the blueprint statement in `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` and the
corresponding Lean declaration in `MIPStarRE/...`. Compare them on every
axis that matters:

- **Quantifiers and hypotheses.** Does every blueprint hypothesis appear
  in the Lean signature, with the same strength? Watch for silent
  weakening ("primitive" in blueprint vs "irreducible" in Lean) or
  silent strengthening ("for all $A$" in blueprint vs implicit
  `[Nontrivial A]`/`[Fintype d]`/etc. in Lean that the blueprint
  omits).
  For a theorem, lemma, or proposition that cites a paper statement,
  an additional bridge, residual, repair, package, producer, witness, wrapper, proof-obligation input, or generic hypotheses bundle, generic assumptions bundle, or arbitrary
  hypothesis input is a mathematical mismatch. The only acceptable extra
  hypotheses are boundary conditions genuinely needed to state the same
  mathematics in Lean, such as positivity for a division, nonemptiness,
  decidability, or a field-model instance. Proof-debt objects are not
  boundary conditions.
  Missing proof work belongs as a tracked `sorry` on the source-faithful
  theorem, as a source-faithful lemma target to be proved from the same
  hypotheses, or as a paper-gap report; it must not become a bundled hypothesis
  consumed by downstream code.  Do not recommend adding a conditional helper
  merely to make a blueprint link pass.  An existing conditional helper may
  remain only as temporary quarantine for already useful proof content, with an
  explicit discharge or deletion plan, and it must stay off the paper theorem's
  `\leanok` path.
- **Conclusion.** Does the blueprint conclusion match the Lean return
  type? Watch for "$X$" vs "$X^\dagger$", "$=$" vs "$\leq$", strict
  vs non-strict inequalities, and conjugate-linear vs linear conventions
  (e.g. `mpvOverlap A B N = star (mpvInner A B N)` — the project's own
  `Fact-Check Lessons` in `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` calls this out).
- **Indexing conventions.** Blueprint indices run 0 to d−1 (matching
  `Fin d`). Flag if the blueprint silently uses 1 to d.
- **Definitions vs theorems.** If the blueprint asserts a fact ("X is a
  subalgebra"), it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not
  `\begin{definition}`.
- **Notation drift.** Does the blueprint use the established notation
  from `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` §"Notation Consistency"? Ad-hoc
  notation that disagrees with the Lean object is a sync bug.

For each mismatch, cite both the blueprint line and the Lean line, and
describe the mathematical discrepancy precisely. Do NOT accept "close
enough" — sync means equivalence, not similarity.

### A.2 — `\leanok` accuracy

`\leanok` on a `\begin{definition}`/`\begin{theorem}`/`\begin{lemma}`
asserts that the *statement* is formalized. `\leanok` inside
`\begin{proof}` asserts that the *proof* is fully formalized.

For every `\leanok` in changed .tex files (and for every newly proven
Lean theorem in the diff that should bear one):

- **Statement `\leanok`** is valid iff `\lean{Name}` resolves AND the
  Lean declaration's signature matches per A.1. If A.1 finds a
  mismatch, the `\leanok` is invalid.
- **Proof `\leanok`** is valid iff the corresponding Lean proof contains
  **no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` on non-trivial goals**, and no
  `axiom` introduced in this PR. Read the Lean proof body and check.
  `grep -n 'sorry\|admit' MIPStarRE/...` is a quick first pass.
- **Missing `\leanok`** is also a sync bug only when the Lean declaration
  is fully formalized, contains no proof-evasion device, and is
  source-faithful under A.1.  Do not recommend `\leanok` for a
  conditional helper that has extra non-paper hypotheses.
- **Open internal obligations** may be linked by `\lean{...}` for
  traceability only when the link clarifies a genuine proof frontier.  They
  must not be placed inside an existing `\leanok` block when they contain
  `sorry`, depend on `sorryAx`, or intentionally represent proof debt.  Do not
  ask authors to create or link conditional helpers merely to avoid a `sorry`;
  the preferred source-realignment repair is the source statement with a
  tracked `sorry`, or the lowest named internal obligation with a tracked
  `sorry`.  If a renamed declaration is still an open obligation, prefer a
  separate remark or implementation note with `\lean{...}` and no `\leanok`.

### A.3 — `\notready` accuracy

`\notready` means "the blueprint entry itself is not yet ready for
formalization" (e.g. statement still being clarified). Flag any
`\notready` on an entry whose Lean counterpart already exists and
matches — the blueprint clearly *is* ready and the tag is stale.

### A.4 — Tag presence and `\uses{...}`

- **New Lean declaration with no blueprint entry**: must add a
  `\begin{definition/theorem/lemma}` block with `\lean{...}`,
  appropriate status tag, and `\uses{...}` for dependencies.
- **Newly closed `sorry`** in Lean: blueprint `\begin{proof}` for that
  theorem must gain `\leanok`.
- **Removed or renamed Lean declaration**: blueprint must drop or
  rename the corresponding `\lean{...}` tag; otherwise
  `leanblueprint checkdecls` will fail.
  If the renamed declaration is an open internal obligation with `sorry`, do
  not demand that it be added to a source-labelled theorem block carrying
  `\leanok`; require only a non-`\leanok` traceability entry when the
  declaration is mathematically useful to mention.
- **`\uses{...}` accuracy**: a proof's `\uses` must match the lemmas the
  Lean proof actually invokes. Do not list everything the statement
  mentions; do not omit lemmas the proof uses.

+\begin{remark}[Normalization of the distance in the linearity conclusion]
+	\label{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}
+	The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} bounds the state-dependent
+	operator distance $d_{\rho'}$ by $\delta$, as quoted in
+	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The calculation behind that bound in
+	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity} computes the distance between
+	the binary projective measurements associated with the observables, which
+	is half the squared operator distance, and then identifies the two
+	quantities; the identification loses that factor. What the Fourier
+	argument proves is the bound $\delta$ for the squared measurement
+	distance, equivalently $2\delta$ for the squared operator distance, and
+	the operator bound $\delta$ stated above is refuted by a four-point
+	counterexample \cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization}. The
+	normalization identities are recorded in
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}; realigning the statement of
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is a separate task.
+\end{remark}

+	\label{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}

+	the finite Fourier identities used in the proof given there for
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}. Write $\chi_u(a) = (-1)^{u \cdot a}$ for
+	$u, a \in \F_2^t$ and, for a family $\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ of operators,
+	set $\widehat{O}^u = \E_a \, \chi_u(a) \, O(a)$. Each $\widehat{O}^u$ is
+	Hermitian when every $O(a)$ is, and for two such families $A$ and $B$,
+	\[
+		O(a) = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, \widehat{O}^u ,

+/-!
+# The operator-valued BLR bound
+
+This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
+linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
+indexed by the Boolean cube `(ZMod 2)^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
+operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
+family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
+sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
+overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` that the
+Naimark dilation consumes.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
+assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
+  from `O^{u+v}`.
+* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
+  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
+  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
+  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
+* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
+  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
+* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
+  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
+
+## References
+
+Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
+its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
+distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
+the theorem at
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
+invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
+the error constant is analyzed in
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
+bound is `2 * δ` for the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for
+the normalized binary-observable distance.
+-/

+/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
+
+/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
+uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `(ZMod 2)^t`, of the real part of
+`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
+Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
+quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
+`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
+the one used there. -/
+def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+    (fun pair =>
+      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
+
+/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
+namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
+`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
+quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
+measured with the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`. -/
+def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

+  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
+
+/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
+defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
+expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
+triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
+adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
+equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
+family. -/
+theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
+    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
+    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
+      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
+  have hu := hO u
+  have hv := hO v
+  have huv := hO (u + v)
+  have hdiff :
+      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
+        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
+      huv.1.eq]
+    calc
+      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
+          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
+            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
+        noncomm_ring
+      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
+            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
+        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
+        module

+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =

+    calc

+        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
+          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
+      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
+        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _

+      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
+        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by

+  rw [hdiff]
+  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
+  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
